summary: Decision: when the baseline ClassifyStance path finds no cue at all and the abstract is non-empty, a non-negated 'X reduces Y' claim reads as supporting at a fixed, lower confidence if a downward finding (reduced, shorter, fewer, less, lower) has the claim's intervention within the pairing window of its sentence and names the claim's head outcome, its last content word, itself (after the cue, or before it as '<outcome> was/were <cue>', with no contrast word or clause break in between), in a sentence that is not framing, 'neither ... nor', a question, locally negated, a 'to' purpose phrase or a modal ('may reduce'), and does not put the lower value in the control arm, compare against the intervention ('than [with] <intervention>'), negate the intervention after the cue, hold a contrast word after the cue, or name the intervention as the comparator in a clause before the cue.
reason: claimBenefitCues and supportCues only know 'reduces the risk', so abstracts reporting 'reduced the duration of Y' scored inconclusive with zero cues. The fallback never runs on harm claims or after any support, null or harm cue, so counting-path results stay as they were.
validated_outcome: 51 invented cases; cases 12-15 RED on the first version, cases 16, 17, 19, 20, 22, 24, 25 RED on the second, cases 26-30, 35, 36 RED on the third, cases 37-42 and 50 RED on the fourth. 306 archived corpus works: 0 changes from a non-inconclusive stance, 1 inconclusive to supporting at 0.6 (vitamind). 18-study chewing-gum/ileus set: all 5 target DOIs move inconclusive to supporting, plus 1 other. Mutations: 30 of 32 caught (both survivors are equivalent: the pairing window's outcome check is implied by the outcome-tie check, and the forward tie's contrast check by the contrast check after the cue), all four comment controls passed.
